The Orange were led by first-year head coach [[Adrian Autry]] and played their home games at [[JMA Wireless Dome]] in [[Syracuse, New York]] as eleventh-year members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. The Syracuse Orange men's basketball team drew an average home attendance of 20,288 in 2023-24, the 2nd highest in college basketball.{{Cite web |title=MEN’S BASKETBALL ATTENDANCE RECORDS THROUGH 2023-24 |url=http://fs.ncaa.org.s3.amazonaws.com/Docs/stats/m_basketball_RB/Attend.pdf |website=NCAA}} The Orange won their first three games of the season before participating in the [[2023 Maui Invitational|Maui Invitational]]. They lost the first two games of the tournament against seventh-ranked [[2023–24 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]] and eleventh-ranked [[2023–24 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]]. They finished the tournament with a win against [[Chaminade Silverswords|Chaminade]]. They followed that with an [[ACC–SEC Challenge]] win against [[2023–24 LSU Tigers men's basketball team|LSU]] before losing their ACC opener to [[2023–24 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]]. The Orange won their final four non-conference games to finish with a non-conference record of 9–2. Syracuse won four of its next six ACC games, including two wins against [[2023–24 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]] and the only losses coming against fourteenth-ranked [[2023–24 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] and seventh-ranked [[2023–24 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]]. The Orange weren't able to carry that momentum forward, as they lost four of their next six games. They rebounded to end their season, winning five of their last seven games, including an upset win over seventh-ranked North Carolina. They completed a season sweep of [[2023–24 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]] but ended the season with a loss as they were beaten by [[2023–24 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]] for the second time in the season. The Orange finished the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] 20–12 and 11–9 in [[2023–24 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a three-way tie for fifth place. Syracuse lost the tiebreaker and was the seventh seed in the [[2024 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]]. They faced tenth-seed NC State for the third time this season in the Second Round and NC State avenged both regular season losses by defeating the Orange 83–65. They were not invited to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and they were eligible to participate in the [[2024 National Invitation Tournament|NIT Tournament]], but they opted not to participate.{{cite web |last1=Waters |first1=Mike |title=Syracuse opted out of NIT prior to selection of tournament field |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2024/03/syracuse-opted-out-of-nit-prior-to-selection-of-tournament-field.html |website= Syracuse.com |access-date=March 17, 2024 |date=March 17, 2024}} ==Previous season== The [[2022–23 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Orange]] finished the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2022–23 season]] 17–15, 10–10 in [[2022–23 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a tie for eighth place. As the eighth seed in the [[2023 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], they lost to [[2022–23 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]] in the second round. This was the second year in a row that Syracuse did not qualify for any post season tournament, a first in then coach Jim Boeheim's 47 year tenure.{{cite
